paragraphs: Friend, this passage is a LONG list of names, and I want you to see what the list is telling us. Twelve divisions took turns serving the king, one month each, and every division had a commander in charge (1 Chronicles 27:1-15). Leaders are listed over many of the tribes, and officials are listed over King David's storehouses, fields, vineyards and herds (1 Chronicles 27:16-22, 25-31). Somebody's name is written next to every job on that list.

Now look at the one spot where the list stops. David did not count the men aged twenty or under, because "the LORD had said that He would make Israel as numerous as the stars of the sky" (1 Chronicles 27:23). Joab began a count and did not finish, and wrath came upon Israel because of it (1 Chronicles 27:24). Even in a list full of order, the lesson is that Israel's strength was never in the numbers. It was in what the LORD had said. So when you plan, and you SHOULD plan, friend, don't trust the plan more than you trust His word.

Here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today. God's work gets done through ordinary people with ordinary jobs, one month and one field at a time. Somebody watched the camels. Somebody was the king's friend (1 Chronicles 27:30, 33). I think a job that looks small on paper still matters when it's done faithfully, and I bet you have a job like that right now. Keep your oven ready and do your part, friend.
